blocks.text: An Architectural Draftsman prepares technical drawings and documentation used to communicate building designs to clients, architects, engineers and construction teams. The role involves translating design concepts into floor plans, elevations, sections, details and drawing sets using manual drafting methods and computer-aided design software.

A diploma in Architecture Assistantship or Interior Design can provide a foundation for drafting-related roles. Depending on the programme, graduates may work on building layouts, interior plans, furniture layouts, door and window schedules, construction details and presentation drawings.

Architectural Draftsmen generally work under the direction of architects, interior designers or other qualified professionals. Preparing drawings does not automatically authorize someone to independently approve designs, sign regulated documents or provide professional architectural services where a specific qualification or registration is required.

rows.text: Develop drafting fundamentals, AutoCAD proficiency, building-plan reading and technical documentation. Enter a junior drafting role.
Prepare more complex drawing sets, coordinate design revisions and develop proficiency in 3D modelling or BIM tools.
Specialize in BIM documentation, construction detailing, interior drafting, residential projects or commercial building documentation.
Potentially progress into Senior Architectural Draftsman, BIM Coordinator, CAD Manager, Design Documentation Lead or an independent drafting-services business, subject to applicable rules.

blocks.text: Career progression depends on software proficiency, drawing accuracy, project experience and the ability to coordinate revisions with design and construction teams.

Diploma programmes commonly take two to three years, depending on the qualification and institution. The following roadmap uses a three-year learning structure; adapt it to the actual programme duration.

blocks.text: Draftsmen should work from approved design instructions and flag inconsistencies. Structural calculations, code compliance decisions and regulated approvals must be handled by appropriately qualified professionals.

blocks.label: Project 1
blocks.text: Residential Floor Plan
Prepare a dimensioned floor plan for a small house, including room labels, doors, windows, circulation and basic furniture placement.

blocks.label: Skills
blocks.text: AutoCAD, space planning, dimensions and architectural conventions.

blocks.label: Project 2
blocks.text: Elevations, Sections and Construction Details
Develop front and side elevations, a building section and selected details from a sample design brief.

blocks.label: Skills
blocks.text: orthographic drawing, construction representation and technical detailing.

blocks.label: Project 3
blocks.text: BIM Model and Drawing Sheets
Create a basic residential building model in Revit or comparable BIM software and generate plans, sections, elevations and schedules.

blocks.label: Skills
blocks.text: BIM fundamentals, model organization and drawing documentation.

blocks.label: Project 4
blocks.text: Drawing Revision and Quality-Control Exercise
Review a sample drawing set, identify missing dimensions or inconsistent annotations, and prepare a revision log.

blocks.label: Skills
blocks.text: drawing accuracy, document control and quality checking.

blocks.text: By graduation and initial practical training, aim to demonstrate:

blocks.label: Drafting fundamentals
blocks.text: plans, elevations, sections, dimensions and construction details.

blocks.label: Software
blocks.text: strong AutoCAD proficiency and introductory Revit/BIM skills.

blocks.label: Building knowledge
blocks.text: materials, construction components and architectural conventions.

blocks.label: Documentation
blocks.text: drawing registers, sheet setup, revision control and PDF issue preparation.

blocks.label: Coordination
blocks.text: incorporate approved comments from architects, structural engineers and MEP teams.

blocks.label: Quality control
blocks.text: check dimensions, annotations, drawing consistency and missing information.

blocks.label: Portfolio
blocks.text: at least three well-organized drawing packages showing different building or interior projects.

blocks.label: Professional boundaries
blocks.text: understand when a design issue requires review or approval by a qualified professional.
A strong entry-level candidate should be able to:

items.text: Prepare dimensioned architectural floor plans using CAD software.
Produce elevations, sections and selected construction details.
Interpret architectural drawings and basic building specifications.
Apply layers, scales, symbols and annotation conventions consistently.
Create a basic building model using Revit or comparable software.
Manage drawing revisions and maintain organized project files.
Coordinate drawing changes with architects and other project professionals.
Present a portfolio demonstrating accuracy, clarity and drafting discipline.

blocks.label: Recommended path

blocks.text: The strongest candidates combine precise technical drawing, practical construction knowledge, software proficiency and disciplined document control. Build a portfolio of complete drawing sets—not just isolated plans—and learn BIM tools to expand opportunities in modern architectural and construction documentation.
